```go
type Node struct {
    left, right *Node
    item        int
}

func bottomUpTree(item, depth int) *Node {
    if depth > 0 {
        return &Node{bottomUpTree(2*item-1, depth-1), bottomUpTree(2*item, depth-1), item}
    }
    return &Node{nil, nil, item}
}

func itemCheck(node *Node) int {

        return node.item
    }
    return node.item + itemCheck(node.left) - itemCheck(node.right)
```

```javascript
function stripFasta(src) {
  const n = src.length;
  // collect '>' positions (single forward pass; FASTA has only a few)
  const gts = [];
  let gp = 0;
  while ((gp = src.indexOf(62, gp)) !== -1) { gts.push(gp); gp++; }
  const dst = Buffer.allocUnsafe(n);
  let w = 0, pos = 0, gi = 0;
  while (pos < n) {
    const nl = src.indexOf(10, pos);
    const limit = nl === -1 ? n : nl;
    while (gi < gts.length && gts[gi] < pos) gi++;
    const g = gi < gts.length && gts[gi] < limit ? gts[gi] : -1;
    if (g === -1) {
      src.copy(dst, w, pos, limit);
      w += limit - pos;
      if (nl === -1) break;
      pos = nl + 1;
    } else if (nl === -1) {
      src.copy(dst, w, pos);
      w += n - pos;
      break;
    } else {
      src.copy(dst, w, pos, g);
      w += g - pos;
      pos = nl + 1;
    }
  }
  return dst.subarray(0, w);
}
```

```javascript
/*
 * regex-redux — Computer Language Benchmarks Game.
 *
 * The harness runs `node regex-redux.js N` with a FASTA stream on stdin.
 * N only controls the upstream fasta generator, so it is parsed for
 * contract compliance but the result depends solely on stdin.
 *
 * Implementation notes (performance):
 *  - Everything is done on raw bytes (Buffer). FASTA is ASCII, so one byte
 *    equals one character and all lengths are byte counts.
 *  - Header/newline stripping, the nine match counts and the five
 *    substitutions are performed with memchr/memmem based scans
 *    (Buffer.indexOf) plus byte-wise verification instead of the regex
 *    engine, which avoids backtracking overhead and intermediate strings.
 *  - Each regex alternative used here is a fixed template with at most one
 *    single-character class; it is matched by anchoring on its longer
 *    literal part and verifying the remaining positions.
 *  - The substitution patterns are expanded to plain literals
 *    (e.g. tHa[Nt] -> tHaN | tHat) so they need no verification at all.
 *  - Leftmost, non-overlapping, alternation-in-order semantics of a global
 *    regex scan are replicated exactly by a candidate-cache matcher.
 */

const fs = require('fs');

if (process.argv.length > 2) parseInt(process.argv[2], 10); // N (unused)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- read input
const input = fs.readFileSync(0);
const originalLength = input.length;

// ------------------------------------------- strip />.*\n/ and every '\n'
function stripFasta(src) {
  const n = src.length;
  const dst = Buffer.allocUnsafe(n);
  let w = 0;

  // Positions of all '>' bytes (a single forward memchr pass; FASTA has few).
  const gts = [];
  for (let gp = src.indexOf(62); gp !== -1; gp = src.indexOf(62, gp + 1)) {
    gts.push(gp);
  }

  let gi = 0;
  for (let pos = 0; pos < n; ) {
    const nl = src.indexOf(10, pos);              // next '\n' from pos
    const limit = nl === -1 ? n : nl;
    while (gi < gts.length && gts[gi] < pos) gi++;
    const g = gi < gts.length && gts[gi] < limit ? gts[gi] : -1;
    if (g === -1) {
      // no '>' before the next newline: keep the data, drop the '\n'
      src.copy(dst, w, pos, limit);
      w += limit - pos;
      if (nl === -1) break;
      pos = nl + 1;
    } else if (nl === -1) {
      // '>' but no newline afterwards: />.*\n/ cannot match and no '\n'
      // remains, so the tail is kept verbatim.
      src.copy(dst, w, pos);
      w += n - pos;
      break;
    } else {
      // header: keep [pos, g), drop [g, nl] ('>' through '\n')
      src.copy(dst, w, pos, g);
      w += g - pos;
      pos = nl + 1;
    }
  }
  return dst.subarray(0, w);
}

// ------------------------------------------------- alternative descriptors
// Shape (identical key order for all): anchor, off, len, clsPos, c0, c1, c2, checks

  return {
    anchor: Buffer.from(str, 'latin1'),
    off: 0,
    len: str.length,
    clsPos: -1,
    c0: 0,
    c1: 0,
    c2: 0,
    checks: [],
  };
}
```

```javascript
'use strict';

// regex-redux (Computer Language Benchmarks Game)
//
// Invoked as `node regex-redux.js N` with the FASTA data piped to stdin.
// N only sizes the upstream fasta generator, so it is parsed for contract
// compliance but the answer depends solely on the bytes read from stdin.
//
// The whole pipeline runs on raw bytes (FASTA is ASCII: 1 byte == 1 char,
// so every length is a byte count).  Header/newline stripping, the nine
// match counts and the five substitutions use memchr/memmem scans
// (Buffer.indexOf) with byte-wise verification instead of the regex engine:
// every pattern alternative is a fixed template with at most one
// single-character class, so it can be matched by anchoring on its longer
// literal part.  Substitution patterns are expanded to plain literals
// (tHa[Nt] -> tHaN | tHat, ...).  A candidate-cache matcher reproduces the
// exact leftmost / non-overlapping / alternation-order semantics of a
// global regex scan without backtracking or intermediate strings.

const fs = require('fs');

// N (argv[2]) is unused here; parse it to honour the invocation contract.
if (process.argv.length > 2) parseInt(process.argv[2], 10);

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ input
const input = fs.readFileSync(0);
const originalLength = input.length;

// ------------------------------------------- strip />.*\n/ and every \n
function stripFasta(src) {
  const n = src.length;
  const dst = Buffer.allocUnsafe(n);
  let w = 0;

  // One forward memchr pass collects every '>' (FASTA has only a few).
  const gts = [];
  for (let gp = src.indexOf(62); gp !== -1; gp = src.indexOf(62, gp + 1)) {
    gts.push(gp);
  }

  let gi = 0;
  for (let pos = 0; pos < n; ) {
    const nl = src.indexOf(10, pos); // next '\n' at or after pos
    const limit = nl === -1 ? n : nl;
    while (gi < gts.length && gts[gi] < pos) gi++;
    const g = gi < gts.length && gts[gi] < limit ? gts[gi] : -1;
    if (g === -1) {
      // data up to the newline: keep it, drop the newline
      src.copy(dst, w, pos, limit);
      w += limit - pos;
      if (nl === -1) break;
      pos = nl + 1;
    } else if (nl === -1) {
      // '>' with no newline after it: />.*\n/ cannot match and no '\n'
      // is left, so the tail is kept verbatim.
      src.copy(dst, w, pos);
      w += n - pos;
      break;
    } else {
      // header line: keep [pos, g), drop [g, nl] ('>' .. '\n' inclusive)
      src.copy(dst, w, pos, g);
      w += g - pos;
      pos = nl + 1;
    }
  }
  return dst.subarray(0, w);
}

const seq = stripFasta(input);
const strippedLength = seq.length;

// ---------------------------------------------------- alternative lookup
// All descriptor objects share one hidden class (same key order).
function litAlt(str) {
  return {
    anchor: Buffer.from(str, 'latin1'),
    off: 0,
    len: str.length,
    clsPos: -1,
    c0: 0,
    c1: 0,
    c2: 0,
    checks: [],
  };
}

// template: pattern text with '?' at clsPos; clsChars: the 3 class members.
function clsAlt(template, clsPos, clsChars) {
  const prefix = template.slice(0, clsPos);
  const suffix = template.slice(clsPos + 1);
  let anchorStr;
  let off;
  const checks = [];
  if (prefix.length >= suffix.length) {
    anchorStr = prefix;
    off = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < suffix.length; i++) {
      checks.push(clsPos + 1 + i, suffix.charCodeAt(i));
    }
  } else {
    anchorStr = suffix;
    off = clsPos + 1;
    for (let i = 0; i < prefix.length; i++) {
      checks.push(i, prefix.charCodeAt(i));
    }
  }
  return {
    anchor: Buffer.from(anchorStr, 'latin1'),
    off: off,
    len: template.length,
    clsPos: clsPos,
    c0: clsChars.charCodeAt(0),
    c1: clsChars.charCodeAt(1),
    c2: clsChars.charCodeAt(2),
    checks: checks,
  };
}

// Smallest match of `alt` starting at or after `from` (-1 if none).
function findNext(src, from, alt) {
  let r = src.indexOf(alt.anchor, from + alt.off);
  while (r !== -1) {
    const q = r - alt.off;
    if (alt.clsPos >= 0) {
      const c = src[q + alt.clsPos];
      if (c !== alt.c0 && c !== alt.c1 && c !== alt.c2) {
        r = src.indexOf(alt.anchor, r + 1);
        continue;
      }
    }
    const chk = alt.checks;
    let ok = true;
    for (let i = 0; i < chk.length; i += 2) {
      if (src[q + chk[i]] !== chk[i + 1]) {
        ok = false;
        break;
      }
    }
    if (ok) return q;
    r = src.indexOf(alt.anchor, r + 1);
  }
  return -1;
}

// Leftmost non-overlapping matches of the alternation `alts` (tried in
// order, exactly like a global regex scan).  Returns the match count and,
// when `out` is an array, also pushes flat (position, length) pairs.
function runMatches(src, alts, out) {
  const k = alts.length;
  const cand = new Array(k);
  for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) cand[i] = findNext(src, 0, alts[i]);
  let count = 0;
  while (true) {
    let best = -1;
    let bi = -1;
    for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) {
      const c = cand[i];
      if (c !== -1 && (bi === -1 || c < best)) {
        best = c;
        bi = i;
      }
    }
    if (bi === -1) return count;
    count++;
    if (out !== null) out.push(best, alts[bi].len);
    const np = best + alts[bi].len;
    for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) {
      if (cand[i] !== -1 && cand[i] < np) cand[i] = findNext(src, np, alts[i]);
    }
  }
}

const patterns = [
  ['agggtaaa|tttaccct',
    [litAlt('agggtaaa'), litAlt('tttaccct')]],
  ['[cgt]gggtaaa|tttaccc[acg]',
    [clsAlt('?gggtaaa', 0, 'cgt'), clsAlt('tttaccc?', 7, 'acg')]],
  ['a[act]ggtaaa|tttacc[agt]t',
    [clsAlt('a?ggtaaa', 1, 'act'), clsAlt('tttacc?t', 6, 'agt')]],
  ['ag[act]gtaaa|tttac[agt]ct',
    [clsAlt('ag?gtaaa', 2, 'act'), clsAlt('tttac?ct', 5, 'agt')]],
  ['agg[act]taaa|ttta[agt]cct',
    [clsAlt('agg?taaa', 3, 'act'), clsAlt('ttta?cct', 4, 'agt')]],
  ['aggg[acg]aaa|ttt[cgt]ccct',
    [clsAlt('aggg?aaa', 4, 'acg'), clsAlt('ttt?ccct', 3, 'cgt')]],
  ['agggt[cgt]aa|tt[acg]accct',
    [clsAlt('agggt?aa', 5, 'cgt'), clsAlt('tt?accct', 2, 'acg')]],
  ['agggta[cgt]a|t[acg]taccct',
    [clsAlt('agggta?a', 6, 'cgt'), clsAlt('t?taccct', 1, 'acg')]],
  ['agggtaa[cgt]|[acg]ttaccct',
    [clsAlt('agggtaa?', 7, 'cgt'), clsAlt('?ttaccct', 0, 'acg')]],
];

const lines = [];
for (let i = 0; i < patterns.length; i++) {
  lines.push(patterns[i][0] + ' ' + runMatches(seq, patterns[i][1], null));
}

// --------------------------------------------------------- substitutions
function replaceFixed(src, alts, rep) {
  const matches = [];
  runMatches(src, alts, matches);
  if (matches.length === 0) return src;
  let dstLen = src.length;
  for (let i = 1; i < matches.length; i += 2) dstLen += rep.length - matches[i];
  const dst = Buffer.allocUnsafe(dstLen);
  let w = 0;
  let epos = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < matches.length; i += 2) {
    const p = matches[i];
    src.copy(dst, w, epos, p);
    w += p - epos;
    rep.copy(dst, w);
    w += rep.length;
    epos = p + matches[i + 1];
  }
  src.copy(dst, w, epos);
  return dst;
}

// spans: inclusive [start, end] pairs, each replaced by the single byte.
function buildSpans(src, spans, repByte) {
  if (spans.length === 0) return src;
  let dstLen = src.length;
  for (let i = 0; i < spans.length; i += 2) dstLen -= spans[i + 1] - spans[i];
  const dst = Buffer.allocUnsafe(dstLen);
  let w = 0;
  let epos = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < spans.length; i += 2) {
    const s = spans[i];
    const e = spans[i + 1];
    src.copy(dst, w, epos, s);
    w += s - epos;
    dst[w++] = repByte;
    epos = e + 1;
  }
  src.copy(dst, w, epos);
  return dst;
}

// /<[^>]*>/g -> '|'
function replaceTag(src) {
  const spans = [];
  for (let scan = 0; ; ) {
    const lt = src.indexOf(60, scan);
    if (lt === -1) break;
    const gt = src.indexOf(62, lt + 1);
    if (gt === -1) break;
    spans.push(lt, gt);
    scan = gt + 1;
  }
  return buildSpans(src, spans, 124);
}

// /\|[^|][^|]*\|/g -> '-'
function replacePipes(src) {
  const spans = [];
  for (let scan = 0; ; ) {
    const a = src.indexOf(124, scan);
    if (a === -1) break;
    const b = src.indexOf(124, a + 1);
    if (b === -1) break;
    if (b - a >= 2) {
      spans.push(a, b);
      scan = b + 1;
    } else {
      scan = a + 1; // '||' cannot start a match; retry at the second pipe
    }
  }
  return buildSpans(src, spans, 45);
}

let cur = seq;
// tHa[Nt] -> <4>
cur = replaceFixed(cur, [litAlt('tHaN'), litAlt('tHat')], Buffer.from('<4>', 'latin1'));
// aND|caN|Ha[DS]|WaS -> <3>
cur = replaceFixed(
  cur,
  [litAlt('aND'), litAlt('caN'), litAlt('HaD'), litAlt('HaS'), litAlt('WaS')],
  Buffer.from('<3>', 'latin1')
);
// a[NSt]|BY -> <2>
cur = replaceFixed(cur, [litAlt('aN'), litAlt('aS'), litAlt('aT'), litAlt('BY')], Buffer.from('<2>', 'latin1'));
// <[^>]*> -> |
cur = replaceTag(cur);
// \|[^|][^|]*\| -> -
cur = replacePipes(cur);
const finalLength = cur.length;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- output
lines.push('');
lines.push(String(originalLength));
lines.push(String(strippedLength));
lines.push(String(finalLength));
process.stdout.write(lines.join('\n') + '\n');
```

'use strict';

/*
 * regex-redux — Computer Language Benchmarks Game.
 *
 * Run as `node regex-redux.js N` with the FASTA stream piped to stdin.
 * N only controls the upstream fasta generator, so it is parsed to honour
 * the invocation contract, but the answer depends solely on stdin.
 *
 * Everything is processed as raw bytes (FASTA is ASCII, so 1 byte == 1
 * character and every length is a byte count).  Header/newline stripping,
 * the nine match counts and the five substitutions are done with
 * memchr/memmem scans (Buffer.indexOf) plus byte-wise verification instead
 * of the backtracking regex engine:
 *   - every counting alternative is a fixed template with at most one
 *     single-character class; it is matched by anchoring a memmem search on
 *     its longer literal part and verifying the remaining bytes;
 *   - the substitution patterns expand to plain literals
 *     (tHa[Nt] -> tHaN|tHat, Ha[DS] -> HaD|HaS, a[NSt] -> aN|aS|aT);
 *   - <[^>]*> and \|[^|][^|]*\| reduce to "first '>' / '|' after the
 *     opener" span scans;
 *   - a candidate-cache matcher reproduces the exact leftmost,
 *     non-overlapping, alternation-in-order behaviour of a global regex.
 */

const fs = require('fs');

// N (argv[2]) is not used by this benchmark; parse it for the contract.
if (process.argv.length > 2) parseInt(process.argv[2], 10);

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ input
const input = fs.readFileSync(0);
const originalLength = input.length;

// ------------------------------------------ strip />.*\n/ and every '\n'
function stripFasta(src) {
  const n = src.length;
  const dst = Buffer.allocUnsafe(n);
  let w = 0;

  // One forward memchr pass collects every '>' (FASTA has only a few).
  const gts = [];
  for (let gp = src.indexOf(62); gp !== -1; gp = src.indexOf(62, gp + 1)) {
    gts.push(gp);
  }

  let gi = 0;
  for (let pos = 0; pos < n; ) {
    const nl = src.indexOf(10, pos); // next '\n' at or after pos
    const limit = nl === -1 ? n : nl;
    while (gi < gts.length && gts[gi] < pos) gi++;
    const g = gi < gts.length && gts[gi] < limit ? gts[gi] : -1;
    if (g === -1) {
      // no '>' before the next newline: keep the data, drop the '\n'
      src.copy(dst, w, pos, limit);
      w += limit - pos;
      if (nl === -1) break;
      pos = nl + 1;
    } else if (nl === -1) {
      // '>' with no newline after it: />.*\n/ cannot match and no '\n'
      // remains, so the tail is kept verbatim.
      src.copy(dst, w, pos);
      w += n - pos;
      break;
    } else {
      // header line: keep [pos, g), drop [g, nl] ('>' through '\n')
      src.copy(dst, w, pos, g);
      w += g - pos;
      pos = nl + 1;
    }
  }
  return dst.subarray(0, w);
}

const seq = stripFasta(input);
const strippedLength = seq.length;

// ---------------------------------------------------- alternative lookup
// All descriptors share one hidden class (identical key order).
function litAlt(str) {
  return {
    anchor: Buffer.from(str, 'latin1'),
    off: 0,
    len: str.length,
    clsPos: -1,
    c0: 0,
    c1: 0,
    c2: 0,
    checks: [],
  };
}

// template: pattern text with '?' at clsPos; clsChars: the class members.
function clsAlt(template, clsPos, clsChars) {
  const prefix = template.slice(0, clsPos);
  const suffix = template.slice(clsPos + 1);
  let anchorStr;
  let off;
  const checks = [];
  if (prefix.length >= suffix.length) {
    anchorStr = prefix;
    off = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < suffix.length; i++) {
      checks.push(clsPos + 1 + i, suffix.charCodeAt(i));
    }
  } else {
    anchorStr = suffix;
    off = clsPos + 1;
    for (let i = 0; i < prefix.length; i++) {
      checks.push(i, prefix.charCodeAt(i));
    }
  }
  return {
    anchor: Buffer.from(anchorStr, 'latin1'),
    off: off,
    len: template.length,
    clsPos: clsPos,
    c0: clsChars.charCodeAt(0),
    c1: clsChars.charCodeAt(1),
    c2: clsChars.charCodeAt(2),
    checks: checks,
  };
}

// Smallest match of `alt` starting at or after `from` (-1 if none).
function findNext(src, from, alt) {
  let r = src.indexOf(alt.anchor, from + alt.off);
  while (r !== -1) {
    const q = r - alt.off;
    if (alt.clsPos >= 0) {
      const c = src[q + alt.clsPos];
      if (c !== alt.c0 && c !== alt.c1 && c !== alt.c2) {
        r = src.indexOf(alt.anchor, r + 1);
        continue;
      }

    const chk = alt.checks;
    let ok = true;
    for (let i = 0; i < chk.length; i += 2) {

        ok = false;
        break;
      }
    }
    if (ok) return q;
    r = src.indexOf(alt.anchor, r + 1);
  }
  return -1;

// Leftmost non-overlapping matches of the alternation `alts`, tried in
// order exactly like a global regex scan.  Returns the match count and,
// when `out` is an array, also pushes flat (position, length) pairs.
function runMatches(src, alts, out) {
  const k = alts.length;
  const cand = new Array(k);
  for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) cand[i] = findNext(src, 0, alts[i]);
  let count = 0;
  while (true) {
    let best = -1;
    let bi = -1;
    for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) {
      const c = cand[i];
      if (c !== -1 && (bi === -1 || c < best)) {
        best = c;
        bi = i;
      }
    }
    if (bi === -1) return count;
    count++;
    if (out !== null) out.push(best, alts[bi].len);
    const np = best + alts[bi].len;
    for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) {
      if (cand[i] !== -1 && cand[i] < np) cand[i] = findNext(src, np, alts[i]);
    }
  }

  const matches = [];

  if (matches.length === 0) return src;
  let dstLen = src.length;
  for (let i = 1; i < matches.length; i += 2) dstLen += rep.length - matches[i];

    w += p - epos;
    rep.copy(dst, w);
    w += rep.length;
    epos = p + matches[i + 1];

    const e = spans[i + 1];
    src.copy(dst, w, epos, s);
    w += s - epos;
    dst[w++] = repByte;
    epos = e + 1;

```javascript
'use strict';

const fs = require('fs');

function main() {
    // N is accepted as the first CLI argument (per the harness contract).
    // The DNA data itself arrives on stdin, so N is parsed but not needed
    // for the computation.
    const N = parseInt(process.argv[2], 10);
    void N;

    // ---- read the whole FASTA stream ------------------------------------
    const input = fs.readFileSync(0);
    const inLen = input.length;

    // ---- locate the ">THREE" section ------------------------------------
    let dataStart = -1;
    {
        let pos = 0;
        while (pos < inLen) {
            const nl = input.indexOf(0x0a, pos);            // '\n'
            const lineEnd = nl === -1 ? inLen : nl;
            if (
                lineEnd - pos >= 6 &&
                input[pos] === 0x3e &&                      // '>'
                input[pos + 1] === 0x54 &&                  // 'T'
                input[pos + 2] === 0x48 &&                  // 'H'
                input[pos + 3] === 0x52 &&                  // 'R'
                input[pos + 4] === 0x45 &&                  // 'E'
                input[pos + 5] === 0x45                     // 'E'
            ) {
                dataStart = nl === -1 ? inLen : nl + 1;
                break;
            }
            if (nl === -1) break;
            pos = nl + 1;
        }
    }
    if (dataStart < 0) {
```

```javascript
'use strict';

/*
 * k-nucleotide (Benchmarks Game)
 *
 * Reads a FASTA-formatted stream from stdin, extracts the sequence of the
 * ">THREE" section, normalizes it to upper case and reports:
 *
 *   - percentage frequencies of all 1-mers  (descending count, then name)
 *   - percentage frequencies of all 2-mers  (descending count, then name)
 *   - occurrence counts of GGT, GGTA, GGTATT, GGTATTTTAATT,
 *     GGTATTTTAATTTATAGT  (as "<count>\t<fragment>")
 *
 * The sequence length parameter N is accepted as the first command line
 * argument (the DNA data itself arrives on stdin).
 */

const fs = require('fs');

function main() {
    // Harness contract: N is the first command-line argument.  The sequence
    // is piped in on stdin, so N is parsed but not used for the computation.
    const N = parseInt(process.argv[2], 10);
    void N;

    const input = fs.readFileSync(0);
    const inLen = input.length;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Locate the ">THREE" section.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let dataStart = -1;
    {
        let from = 0;
        for (;;) {
            const idx = input.indexOf('>THREE', from);
            if (idx === -1) break;
            if (idx === 0 || input[idx - 1] === 0x0a || input[idx - 1] === 0x0d) {
                const nl = input.indexOf(0x0a, idx);
                dataStart = nl === -1 ? inLen : nl + 1;
                break;
            }
            from = idx + 1;
        }
    }
    if (dataStart < 0) {
        // No explicit ">THREE" header: fall back to the last header section,
        // or to the whole input when the stream has no headers at all.
        const gt = input.lastIndexOf(0x3e);
        if (gt === -1) {
            dataStart = 0;
        } else {
            const nl = input.indexOf(0x0a, gt);
            dataStart = nl === -1 ? inLen : nl + 1;
        }
    }
    const nextHeader = input.indexOf(0x3e, dataStart);
    const dataEnd = nextHeader === -1 ? inLen : nextHeader;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Normalize: upper case, no line breaks.  Bases are kept as small
    // integer codes (A=0, C=1, G=2, T=3; anything else gets a fresh code).
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    const byteToCode = new Int16Array(256).fill(-1);
    byteToCode[0x41] = 0; // A
    byteToCode[0x43] = 1; // C
    byteToCode[0x47] = 2; // G
    byteToCode[0x54] = 3; // T
    const codeToByte = new Uint8Array(256);
    codeToByte[0] = 0x41;
    codeToByte[1] = 0x43;
    codeToByte[2] = 0x47;
    codeToByte[3] = 0x54;
    let nb = 4;

    const seq = new Uint8Array(dataEnd - dataStart);
    let L = 0;
    for (let i = dataStart; i < dataEnd; i++) {
        let b = input[i];
        if (b === 0x0a || b === 0x0d) continue;   // strip CR/LF
        if (b >= 0x61 && b <= 0x7a) b -= 0x20;    // to upper case
        let c = byteToCode[b];
        if (c < 0) {
            c = nb++;
            byteToCode[b] = c;
            codeToByte[c] = b;
        }
        seq[L++] = c;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // One pass over the sequence:
    //   * 1-mer and 2-mer counts
    //   * counts of the five fragments, which are nested prefixes of each
    //     other, so a single match attempt per "GGT" position covers all.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    const count1 = new Float64Array(nb);
    const count2 = new Float64Array(nb * nb);
    const frag = new Float64Array(5);

    let prev = -1;
    for (let i = 0; i < L; i++) {
        const c = seq[i];
        count1[c]++;
        if (prev >= 0) count2[prev * nb + c]++;
        prev = c;

        if (c === 2 && i + 3 <= L && seq[i + 1] === 2 && seq[i + 2] === 3) {
            frag[0]++;                                    // GGT
            if (i + 4 <= L && seq[i + 3] === 0) {
                frag[1]++;                                // GGTA
                if (i + 6 <= L && seq[i + 4] === 3 && seq[i + 5] === 3) {
                    frag[2]++;                            // GGTATT
                    if (i + 12 <= L && seq[i + 6] === 3 && seq[i + 7] === 3 &&
                        seq[i + 8] === 0 && seq[i + 9] === 0 &&
                        seq[i + 10] === 3 && seq[i + 11] === 3) {
                        frag[3]++;                        // GGTATTTTAATT
                        if (i + 18 <= L && seq[i + 12] === 3 && seq[i + 13] === 0 &&
                            seq[i + 14] === 3 && seq[i + 15] === 0 &&
                            seq[i + 16] === 2 && seq[i + 17] === 3) {
                            frag[4]++;                    // GGTATTTTAATTTATAGT
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Report.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    const byCountThenName = (a, b) =>
        (b[1] - a[1]) || (a[0] < b[0] ? -1 : a[0] > b[0] ? 1 : 0);

    const ones = [];
    for (let c = 0; c < nb; c++) {
        if (count1[c] > 0) {
            ones.push([String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[c]), count1[c]]);
        }
    }
    ones.sort(byCountThenName);

    const twos = [];
    for (let p = 0; p < nb; p++) {
        const chP = String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[p]);
        const base = p * nb;
        for (let c = 0; c < nb; c++) {
            const v = count2[base + c];
            if (v > 0) {
                twos.push([chP + String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[c]), v]);
            }
        }
    }
    twos.sort(byCountThenName);

    const out = [];
    for (let k = 0; k < ones.length; k++) {
        out.push(ones[k][0] + ' ' + (ones[k][1] * 100 / L).toFixed(3));
    }
    out.push('');
    const total2 = L > 1 ? L - 1 : 1;
    for (let k = 0; k < twos.length; k++) {
        out.push(twos[k][0] + ' ' + (twos[k][1] * 100 / total2).toFixed(3));
    }
    out.push('');

    const names = ['GGT', 'GGTA', 'GGTATT', 'GGTATTTTAATT', 'GGTATTTTAATTTATAGT'];
    for (let k = 0; k < names.length; k++) {
        out.push(frag[k] + '\t' + names[k]);
    }
    process.stdout.write(out.join('\n') + '\n');
}

main();
```

```javascript
/*
 * k-nucleotide — Benchmarks Game
 *
 * stdin : FASTA-formatted DNA (the stream produced by the fasta benchmark).
 *         The ">THREE" section is the sequence of interest.
 * argv  : N (the sequence-length parameter; the data itself comes from stdin)

 *         occurrence counts of five specific fragments as "<count>\t<name>".

    // The DNA sequence is piped in on stdin, so N itself is not needed here.

    void N;

    const input = fs.readFileSync(0);
    const inLen = input.length;

    // ---- locate the ">THREE" section -------------------------------------
    let dataStart = -1;
    {
        let from = 0;
        for (;;) {
            const idx = input.indexOf('>THREE', from);
            if (idx < 0) break;
            if (idx === 0 || input[idx - 1] === 0x0a || input[idx - 1] === 0x0d) {
                const nl = input.indexOf(0x0a, idx);
                dataStart = nl < 0 ? inLen : nl + 1;
                break;
            }
            from = idx + 1;
        }
    }
    if (dataStart < 0) {
        // Fallback (no ">THREE" header present): use the last header section,
        // or the entire input when the stream contains no header at all.
        const gt = input.lastIndexOf(0x3e);
        if (gt < 0) {
            dataStart = 0;
        } else {
            const nl = input.indexOf(0x0a, gt);
            dataStart = nl < 0 ? inLen : nl + 1;
        }
    }
    const nextHdr = input.indexOf(0x3e, dataStart);
    const dataEnd = nextHdr < 0 ? inLen : nextHdr;

    // ---- normalize: upper case, line breaks removed, packed as codes -----
    // A=0, C=1, G=2, T=3; any other symbol gets a fresh code on first sight.
    const byteToCode = new Int16Array(256).fill(-1);
    byteToCode[0x41] = 0; byteToCode[0x43] = 1; byteToCode[0x47] = 2; byteToCode[0x54] = 3;
    const codeToByte = new Uint8Array(256);
    codeToByte[0] = 0x41; codeToByte[1] = 0x43; codeToByte[2] = 0x47; codeToByte[3] = 0x54;
    let nb = 4;

    const seq = new Uint8Array(dataEnd - dataStart);
    let L = 0;
    for (let i = dataStart; i < dataEnd; i++) {
        let b = input[i];
        if (b === 0x0a || b === 0x0d) continue;        // strip CR/LF
        if (b >= 0x61 && b <= 0x7a) b -= 0x20;         // to upper case
        let c = byteToCode[b];
        if (c < 0) { c = nb++; byteToCode[b] = c; codeToByte[c] = b; }
        seq[L++] = c;
    }

    // ---- 1-mer and 2-mer counts (single branch-free pass) ----------------
    const count1 = new Float64Array(nb);
    const count2 = new Float64Array(nb * nb);
    if (L > 0) {
        count1[seq[0]]++;
        let prev = seq[0];
        for (let i = 1; i < L; i++) {
            const c = seq[i];
            count1[c]++;
            count2[prev * nb + c]++;
            prev = c;
        }
    }

    // ---- fragment counts ---------------------------------------------------
    // The five fragments are nested prefixes of one another, so every match
    // attempt that starts with "GGT" walks down the whole nest at once.
    // Codes: G=2, T=3, A=0.
    const frag = new Float64Array(5);
    {
        const lim = L - 3;
        for (let i = 0; i <= lim; i++) {
            if (seq[i] === 2 && seq[i + 1] === 2 && seq[i + 2] === 3) {
                frag[0]++;                                        // GGT
                if (i + 4 <= L && seq[i + 3] === 0) {
                    frag[1]++;                                    // GGTA
                    if (i + 6 <= L && seq[i + 4] === 3 && seq[i + 5] === 3) {
                        frag[2]++;                                // GGTATT
                        if (i + 12 <= L && seq[i + 6] === 3 && seq[i + 7] === 3 &&
                            seq[i + 8] === 0 && seq[i + 9] === 0 &&
                            seq[i + 10] === 3 && seq[i + 11] === 3) {
                            frag[3]++;                            // GGTATTTTAATT
                            if (i + 18 <= L && seq[i + 12] === 3 && seq[i + 13] === 0 &&
                                seq[i + 14] === 3 && seq[i + 15] === 0 &&
                                seq[i + 16] === 2 && seq[i + 17] === 3) {
                                frag[4]++;                        // GGTATTTTAATTTATAGT
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // ---- report ------------------------------------------------------------
    const byCountThenName = (a, b) => (b[1] - a[1]) || (a[0] < b[0] ? -1 : a[0] > b[0] ? 1 : 0);

    const ones = [];
    for (let c = 0; c < nb; c++) {
        if (count1[c] > 0) ones.push([String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[c]), count1[c]]);
    }
    ones.sort(byCountThenName);

    const twos = [];
    for (let p = 0; p < nb; p++) {
        const chP = String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[p]);
        const row = p * nb;
        for (let c = 0; c < nb; c++) {
            const v = count2[row + c];
            if (v > 0) twos.push([chP + String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[c]), v]);
        }
    }
    twos.sort(byCountThenName);

    const out = [];
    for (let k = 0; k < ones.length; k++) {
        out.push(ones[k][0] + ' ' + (ones[k][1] * 100 / L).toFixed(3));
    }
    out.push('');
    const total2 = L > 1 ? L - 1 : 1;
    for (let k = 0; k < twos.length; k++) {
        out.push(twos[k][0] + ' ' + (twos[k][1] * 100 / total2).toFixed(3));
    }
    out.push('');

    const names = ['GGT', 'GGTA', 'GGTATT', 'GGTATTTTAATT', 'GGTATTTTAATTTATAGT'];
    for (let k = 0; k < names.length; k++) {
        out.push(frag[k] + '\t' + names[k]);
    }
    process.stdout.write(out.join('\n') + '\n');
```

```javascript
'use strict';

// k-nucleotide (Benchmarks Game)
//
// stdin : FASTA-formatted DNA stream (as produced by the fasta benchmark);
//         the ">THREE" section is the sequence to analyse.
// argv  : N - sequence length parameter (the data itself arrives on stdin).
//
// stdout: 1-mer and 2-mer frequencies as "<name> <pct>" (pct with 3 decimals,
//         sorted by descending count, ties by ascending name), each section
//         followed by a blank line, then the occurrence counts of the five
//         specific fragments as "<count>\t<name>".

const fs = require('fs');

function main() {
    // Harness contract: N is the first command-line argument.  The DNA data
    // is piped in on stdin, so N is parsed but not needed for the computation.
    const N = parseInt(process.argv[2], 10);
    void N;

    // ---- slurp the whole FASTA stream ------------------------------------
    const input = fs.readFileSync(0);
    const inLen = input.length;

    // ---- locate the ">THREE" section -------------------------------------
    let dataStart = -1;
    {
        let from = 0;
        for (;;) {
            const idx = input.indexOf('>THREE', from);
            if (idx < 0) break;
            if (idx === 0 || input[idx - 1] === 0x0a || input[idx - 1] === 0x0d) {
                const nl = input.indexOf(0x0a, idx);
                dataStart = nl < 0 ? inLen : nl + 1;
                break;
            }
            from = idx + 1;
        }
    }
    if (dataStart < 0) {
        // No ">THREE" header: fall back to the last header section, or to
        // the whole input when the stream contains no header at all.
        const gt = input.lastIndexOf(0x3e);
        if (gt < 0) {
            dataStart = 0;
        } else {
            const nl = input.indexOf(0x0a, gt);
            dataStart = nl < 0 ? inLen : nl + 1;
        }
    }
    const nextHdr = input.indexOf(0x3e, dataStart);
    const dataEnd = nextHdr < 0 ? inLen : nextHdr;

    // ---- normalize: upper case, no line breaks, packed as small codes ----
    // A=0, C=1, G=2, T=3; any other symbol gets a fresh code on first sight.
    const byteToCode = new Int16Array(256).fill(-1);
    byteToCode[0x41] = 0; // A
    byteToCode[0x43] = 1; // C
    byteToCode[0x47] = 2; // G
    byteToCode[0x54] = 3; // T
    const codeToByte = new Uint8Array(256);
    codeToByte[0] = 0x41;
    codeToByte[1] = 0x43;
    codeToByte[2] = 0x47;
    codeToByte[3] = 0x54;
    let nb = 4;

    const seq = new Uint8Array(dataEnd - dataStart);
    let L = 0;
    for (let i = dataStart; i < dataEnd; i++) {
        let b = input[i];
        if (b === 0x0a || b === 0x0d) continue;      // strip CR/LF
        if (b >= 0x61 && b <= 0x7a) b -= 0x20;       // to upper case
        let c = byteToCode[b];
        if (c < 0) {
            c = nb++;
            byteToCode[b] = c;
            codeToByte[c] = b;
        }
        seq[L++] = c;
    }

    // ---- 1-mer / 2-mer counts (one branch-free pass) ---------------------
    const count1 = new Float64Array(nb);
    const count2 = new Float64Array(nb * nb);
    if (L > 0) {
        count1[seq[0]]++;
        let prev = seq[0];
        for (let i = 1; i < L; i++) {
            const c = seq[i];
            count1[c]++;
            count2[prev * nb + c]++;
            prev = c;
        }
    }

    // ---- fragment counts --------------------------------------------------
    // The five fragments are nested prefixes of one another, so a match
    // attempt starting at every "GGT" walks the whole nest in one go.
    // Codes: G=2, T=3, A=0.
    const frag = new Float64Array(5);
    {
        const lim = L - 3;
        for (let i = 0; i <= lim; i++) {
            if (seq[i] === 2 && seq[i + 1] === 2 && seq[i + 2] === 3) {
                frag[0]++;                                     // GGT
                if (i + 4 <= L && seq[i + 3] === 0) {
                    frag[1]++;                                 // GGTA
                    if (i + 6 <= L && seq[i + 4] === 3 && seq[i + 5] === 3) {
                        frag[2]++;                             // GGTATT
                        if (i + 12 <= L &&
                            seq[i + 6] === 3 && seq[i + 7] === 3 &&
                            seq[i + 8] === 0 && seq[i + 9] === 0 &&
                            seq[i + 10] === 3 && seq[i + 11] === 3) {
                            frag[3]++;                         // GGTATTTTAATT
                            if (i + 18 <= L &&
                                seq[i + 12] === 3 && seq[i + 13] === 0 &&
                                seq[i + 14] === 3 && seq[i + 15] === 0 &&
                                seq[i + 16] === 2 && seq[i + 17] === 3) {
                                frag[4]++;                     // GGTATTTTAATTTATAGT
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // ---- report ------------------------------------------------------------
    const byCountThenName = (a, b) =>
        (b[1] - a[1]) || (a[0] < b[0] ? -1 : a[0] > b[0] ? 1 : 0);

    const ones = [];
    for (let c = 0; c < nb; c++) {
        if (count1[c] > 0) ones.push([String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[c]), count1[c]]);
    }
    ones.sort(byCountThenName);

    const twos = [];
    for (let p = 0; p < nb; p++) {
        const chP = String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[p]);
        const row = p * nb;
        for (let c = 0; c < nb; c++) {
            const v = count2[row + c];
            if (v > 0) twos.push([chP + String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[c]), v]);
        }
    }
    twos.sort(byCountThenName);

    const out = [];
    for (let k = 0; k < ones.length; k++) {
        out.push(ones[k][0] + ' ' + (ones[k][1] * 100 / L).toFixed(3));
```

```javascript
        let b = input[i];
        if (b === 0x0a || b === 0x0d) continue;         // strip CR/LF
        if (b >= 0x61 && b <= 0x7a) b -= 0x20;          // to upper case
        let c = byteToCode[b];
        if (c < 0) { c = nb++; byteToCode[b] = c; codeToByte[c] = b; }
        seq[L++] = c;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 1-mer and 2-mer counts in a single branch-free pass.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    const count1 = new Float64Array(nb);
    const count2 = new Float64Array(nb * nb);
    if (L > 0) {
        count1[seq[0]]++;
        let prev = seq[0];
        for (let i = 1; i < L; i++) {
            const c = seq[i];
            count1[c]++;
            count2[prev * nb + c]++;
            prev = c;
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Fragment counts.  GGT, GGTA, GGTATT, GGTATTTTAATT and
    // GGTATTTTAATTTATAGT are nested prefixes of each other, so every
    // position that starts a "GGT" walks the whole nest in one go.
    // (Codes: G=2, T=3, A=0.)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    const frag = new Float64Array(5);
    for (let i = 0, lim = L - 3; i <= lim; i++) {
        if (seq[i] === 2 && seq[i + 1] === 2 && seq[i + 2] === 3) {
            frag[0]++;                                            // GGT
            if (i + 4 <= L && seq[i + 3] === 0) {
                frag[1]++;                                        // GGTA
                if (i + 6 <= L && seq[i + 4] === 3 && seq[i + 5] === 3) {
                    frag[2]++;                                    // GGTATT
                    if (i + 12 <= L &&
                        seq[i + 6] === 3 && seq[i + 7] === 3 &&
                        seq[i + 8] === 0 && seq[i + 9] === 0 &&
                        seq[i + 10] === 3 && seq[i + 11] === 3) {
                        frag[3]++;                                // GGTATTTTAATT
                        if (i + 18 <= L &&
                            seq[i + 12] === 3 && seq[i + 13] === 0 &&
                            seq[i + 14] === 3 && seq[i + 15] === 0 &&
                            seq[i + 16] === 2 && seq[i + 17] === 3) {
                            frag[4]++;                            // GGTATTTTAATTTATAGT
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Report.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    const byCountThenName = (a, b) =>
        (b[1] - a[1]) || (a[0] < b[0] ? -1 : a[0] > b[0] ? 1 : 0);

    const ones = [];
    for (let c = 0; c < nb; c++) {
        if (count1[c] > 0) ones.push([String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[c]), count1[c]]);
    }
    ones.sort(byCountThenName);

    const twos = [];
    for (let p = 0; p < nb; p++) {
        const chP = String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[p]);
        const row = p * nb;
        for (let c = 0; c < nb; c++) {
            const v = count2[row + c];
            if (v > 0) twos.push([chP + String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[c]), v]);
        }
    }
    twos.sort(byCountThenName);

    const out = [];
    for (let k = 0; k < ones.length; k++) {
        out.push(ones[k][0] + ' ' + (ones[k][1] * 100 / L).toFixed(3));
    }
    out.push('');
    const total2 = L > 1 ? L - 1 : 1;                    // number of 2-mers
    for (let k = 0; k < twos.length; k++) {
        out.push(twos[k][0] + ' ' + (twos[k][1] * 100 / total2).toFixed(3));
    }
    out.push('');

    const names = ['GGT', 'GGTA', 'GGTATT', 'GGTATTTTAATT', 'GGTATTTTAATTTATAGT'];
    for (let k = 0; k < names.length; k++) {
        out.push(frag[k] + '\t' + names[k]);
    }
    process.stdout.write(out.join('\n') + '\n');
}
```

```javascript
'use strict';

/*
 * k-nucleotide — Computer Language Benchmarks Game
 *
 *   stdin : FASTA-formatted DNA stream, as emitted by the fasta benchmark;
 *           the ">THREE" section holds the sequence to analyse.
 *   argv  : N — length parameter of the fasta run that produced the input
 *           (the DNA data itself arrives on stdin, so N is parsed but the
 *           computation only depends on the piped stream).
 *
 *   stdout: frequencies of all 1-mers and 2-mers, one per line, as
 *           "<name> <percentage>" (3 decimals), sorted by descending count
 *           then ascending name, each block followed by a blank line;
 *           then the occurrence counts of the five specific fragments,
 *           one per line, as "<count>\t<name>".
 */

const fs = require('fs');

function main() {
    // Harness contract: N is the first command-line argument.
    const N = parseInt(process.argv[2], 10);
    void N; // the sequence itself is read from stdin

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Slurp stdin; locate the ">THREE" section.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    const input = fs.readFileSync(0);
    const inLen = input.length;

    let dataStart = -1;
    for (let from = 0; ; ) {
        const idx = input.indexOf('>THREE', from);
        if (idx < 0) break;
        if (idx === 0 || input[idx - 1] === 0x0a || input[idx - 1] === 0x0d) {
            const nl = input.indexOf(0x0a, idx);          // end of the header line
            dataStart = nl < 0 ? inLen : nl + 1;
            break;
        }
        from = idx + 1;
    }
    if (dataStart < 0) {
        // No ">THREE" header: fall back to the last header section, or to
        // the whole input when the stream contains no header at all.
        const gt = input.lastIndexOf(0x3e);
        if (gt < 0) {
            dataStart = 0;
        } else {
            const nl = input.indexOf(0x0a, gt);
            dataStart = nl < 0 ? inLen : nl + 1;
        }
    }
    const nextHdr = input.indexOf(0x3e, dataStart);
    const dataEnd = nextHdr < 0 ? inLen : nextHdr;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Normalize: upper case, line breaks removed; bases packed as codes
    // (A=0, C=1, G=2, T=3).  Any other symbol gets a fresh code so the
    // counting stays correct for arbitrary input.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    const byteToCode = new Int16Array(256).fill(-1);
    byteToCode[0x41] = 0; byteToCode[0x43] = 1; byteToCode[0x47] = 2; byteToCode[0x54] = 3;
    const codeToByte = new Uint8Array(256);
    codeToByte[0] = 0x41; codeToByte[1] = 0x43; codeToByte[2] = 0x47; codeToByte[3] = 0x54;
    let nb = 4;

    const seq = new Uint8Array(dataEnd - dataStart);
    let L = 0;
    for (let i = dataStart; i < dataEnd; i++) {
        let b = input[i];
        if (b === 0x0a || b === 0x0d) continue;           // strip CR/LF
        if (b >= 0x61 && b <= 0x7a) b -= 0x20;            // to upper case
        let c = byteToCode[b];
        if (c < 0) { c = nb++; byteToCode[b] = c; codeToByte[c] = b; }
        seq[L++] = c;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 1-mer and 2-mer counts in one branch-free pass.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    const count1 = new Float64Array(nb);
    const count2 = new Float64Array(nb * nb);
    if (L > 0) {
        count1[seq[0]]++;
        let prev = seq[0];
        for (let i = 1; i < L; i++) {
            const c = seq[i];
            count1[c]++;
            count2[prev * nb + c]++;
            prev = c;
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Fragment counts.  GGT, GGTA, GGTATT, GGTATTTTAATT and
    // GGTATTTTAATTTATAGT are nested prefixes of one another, so each
    // position starting a "GGT" walks the whole nest in a single go.
    // (Codes: G=2, T=3, A=0.)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    const frag = new Float64Array(5);
    for (let i = 0, lim = L - 3; i <= lim; i++) {
        if (seq[i] === 2 && seq[i + 1] === 2 && seq[i + 2] === 3) {
            frag[0]++;                                             // GGT
            if (i + 4 <= L && seq[i + 3] === 0) {
                frag[1]++;                                         // GGTA
                if (i + 6 <= L && seq[i + 4] === 3 && seq[i + 5] === 3) {
                    frag[2]++;                                     // GGTATT
                    if (i + 12 <= L &&
                        seq[i + 6] === 3 && seq[i + 7] === 3 &&
                        seq[i + 8] === 0 && seq[i + 9] === 0 &&
                        seq[i + 10] === 3 && seq[i + 11] === 3) {
                        frag[3]++;                                 // GGTATTTTAATT
                        if (i + 18 <= L &&
                            seq[i + 12] === 3 && seq[i + 13] === 0 &&
                            seq[i + 14] === 3 && seq[i + 15] === 0 &&
                            seq[i + 16] === 2 && seq[i + 17] === 3) {
                            frag[4]++;                             // GGTATTTTAATTTATAGT
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Report.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    const byCountThenName = (a, b) =>
        (b[1] - a[1]) || (a[0] < b[0] ? -1 : a[0] > b[0] ? 1 : 0);

    const ones = [];
    for (let c = 0; c < nb; c++) {
        if (count1[c] > 0) ones.push([String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[c]), count1[c]]);
    }
    ones.sort(byCountThenName);

    const twos = [];
    for (let p = 0; p < nb; p++) {
        const chP = String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[p]);
        const row = p * nb;
        for (let c = 0; c < nb; c++) {
            const v = count2[row + c];
            if (v > 0) twos.push([chP + String.fromCharCode(codeToByte[c]), v]);
        }
    }
    twos.sort(byCountThenName);

    const out = [];
    for (let k = 0; k < ones.length; k++) {
        out.push(ones[k][0] + ' ' + (ones[k][1] * 100 / L).toFixed(3));
    }
    out.push('');
    const total2 = L > 1 ? L - 1 : 1;                       // number of 2-mers
    for (let k = 0; k < twos.length; k++) {
        out.push(twos[k][0] + ' ' + (twos[k][1] * 100 / total2).toFixed(3));
    }
    out.push('');

    const names = ['GGT', 'GGTA', 'GGTATT', 'GGTATTTTAATT', 'GGTATTTTAATTTATAGT'];
    for (let k = 0; k < names.length; k++) {
        out.push(frag[k] + '\t' + names[k]);
    }
    process.stdout.write(out.join('\n') + '\n');
}

main();
```
